synthetic_disclaimer: SYNTHETIC EXERCISE. Panelists are AI-constructed composite personas whose positions are inferred from the published literature. Nothing here is a statement by, or endorsed by, the named individuals or any living person. Names in literature_basis identify the work each composite draws on, not participants in a deliberation.
material: Reproduction of ABM mechanism results (floor/race, graduate-supply shock, actor knockouts, gate clustering) + literature audit (Yoo 2003, Kang, Ghaffarzadegan-Xue-Larson) + citation-claim register

panel.label: Composite drawing on model-based-reasoning and complexity literature
panel.role: Model-class reviewer: which results are imposed by the coded rules vs invariant across a model class
panel.why_seated: The brief turns on whether an ABM result is a discovery or an artifact of the formalization; this composite supplies the model-reasoning checklist.
panel.assigned_prior_question: Q1 (imposed vs discovered), Q3 (is C3 a fair beat)

panel.label: Composite drawing on credential-inflation and positional-competition literature
literature_basis: Brown, Lauder & Ashton, The Global Auction (2011)
panel.role: Credential/novelty reviewer: whether the mechanism claims are new relative to the inflation/positional tradition
panel.why_seated: The paper's intensification claim is the credential-society tradition formalized; this composite states what the tradition already claims.

panel.label: Composite drawing on returns-to-education and education-economics literature
literature_basis: Psacharopoulos & Patrinos, 'Returns to investment in education: a decennial review' (2018)
panel.role: Economist and steel-man for the competitive/human-capital rival
panel.why_seated: C3 claims to separate the account from a competitive market; this composite holds the competitive null at its best.
panel.assigned_prior_question: Q1 (rival fairness), Q3 (fair beat), Q4 (evidence needed)

panel.label: Composite drawing on comparative shadow-education literature (mandatory seat: brief includes tutoring claims)
literature_basis: Bray, comparative shadow-education work (HK, Korea, China, Cambodia, Vietnam)
Bray & Zhang, shadow-education research in China
panel.why_seated: C5 is a tutoring claim; the mandatory shadow-education seat judges the model's gate shares against comparative evidence.
panel.assigned_prior_question: Q1 (is C5 imposed), Q5 (China school-support experiment)

panel.label: Composite drawing on philosophy-of-social-science literature
panel.role: Method/type reviewer: model implication vs world claim; falsifiability; scope conditions
panel.why_seated: The brief's central question — what is imposed by equations — is a philosophy-of-science question about model-to-inference.
panel.assigned_prior_question: Q1 (imposed vs discovered), Q4 (evidence thresholds), Q6 (visibility)

deviation_from_lead_recommendation.lead_recommended: ABM + LABOR + SEA + PHIL functional profiles
deviation_from_lead_recommendation.resolution: The Lead's functional roles are preserved and staffed by AI composites grounded in matching published literature: model-reasoning (PAGE), labor economics and steel-man (PATRINOS), shadow-education domain (BRAY, mandatory), philosophy of social science (CARTWRIGHT). COLLINS is added for the credential-novelty question (Q2) that no other role covers.
deviation_from_lead_recommendation.note: No real person participated. See synthetic_disclaimer.

notes: Panel fixed before reviews were written.
